newsitem.title: USA: Dlr/yen above 113 unacceptable -- ex-MOF official.
newsitem.headline: Dlr/yen above 113 unacceptable -- ex-MOF official.

text.p: A comfortable range for the dollar rests between 100 and 110 yen, according to Toyoo Gyohten, president of Japan's Institute for International Monetary Affairs, adding he would prefer to see the U.S. currency below 113 yen.

"(The dollar at) 113 yen is probably at the edge of the acceptable range," said Gyohten, a former Japanese vice minister of finance for international affairs. Gyohten made his comments after addressing the Japan Society here.

Until now, U.S. and Japanese business leaders and monetary authorities have been happy with the dollar's strength against the yen, Gyohten said. However, he said he was not sure how long that satisfaction might last.
"I personally feel (a yen) exchange rate above 110 would be on the side of being too weak," Gyohten said.
In afternoon U.S. trade on Monday, the dollar was quoted at 113.80/90.
